Regenerated for the healing-extension roster change: `blocks.healing` gained an `extension` descriptor (version/revision/signature, decoded from the addon's registration row) and every `blocks.healing.by_entity` row gained `runs_extension` — GW2EI's `RunningExtension` roster, which the native format previously did not carry at all, leaving EI-shaped consumers unable to tell 'this player's healing numbers are complete' from 'partial, relayed by a peer'. Both are intentional new fields, so byteLength grew by 1563 from the pre-roster baseline. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged) for the 1.2.0 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Determinism verified at each regeneration: two independent captures produced byte-identical output and identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for `blocks.self_effects`: the squad-side counterpart to `blocks.conditions`, carrying per-(squad player, effect) uptime and a fused stack timeline for the 14 conditions plus Stun (872) and Daze (833). It is a new opt-in block gated on the existing `--timeseries` flag, which `--all` turns on, so byteLength grew by 248477. Determinism verified: two independent captures of the new output were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested for the `blocks.self_effects` all-zero drop-rule fix: the pass previously emitted a row for a zero-length buff application, whose fused timeline is `[[0, 0], [t, 0]]` -- two entries, so it slipped past the old `len() < 2` guard -- carrying no information, and in one case an `avg_stacks: 0.0` the schema's own convention says should be omitted rather than reported. The guard now tests for a nonzero stack value, dropping exactly those rows: 345 self_effects rows became 343 (entity 22 buff 738 and entity 34 buff 26766 removed), so byteLength shrank by 521. Elite Insights omits such a buff from `buffUptimes` entirely, and the EI equality oracle is unchanged by this (476 cells, worst duration 0.000500pp, worst intensity 0.000497rel, before and after) because it never compared those keys. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged at 8499154) for the 1.3.0 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested for the GW2 API skill-name fallback: `skill_icons` gained a second generated table, `SKILL_NAMES` (4,610 of the API's 4,702 skills), and `skill_map::resolve_name` now consults it before falling back to the `"Skill <id>"` placeholder — arcdps writes no display name for a skill its client had not cached, which left 61 of this fixture's catalog entries reading `"Skill 14404"` where the skill is Signet of Might. The change is purely additive: it ranks BELOW the log's own table, so it can only displace the placeholder. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.3.0 baseline: exactly 61 leaves moved, every one of them a `catalogs.skills.*.name`, every one from a placeholder to a real GW2 name and none in the other direction. byteLength grew by 203. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for `blocks.squad_buffs`: squad-side uptime for every buff that is neither one of the 12 boons nor a condition/control effect — sigils, relics, food, utilities, auras, signets, trait buffs. Elite Insights keeps that whole population in the same `buffUptimes` array as the boons; this project split it by family and the tail previously had no home at all, which is why axibridge's Special Buffs and Sigil/Relic Uptime sections rendered empty. Unlike `blocks.self_effects` this block is ALWAYS-ON: it emits uptime only, at the cost `blocks.boons`' own always-on half already carries. Regenerated for `cleanses_minions`, a new always-on field on every `blocks.support.by_entity` row (and on the EI-shaped export as `condiCleanseMinions`): the count of conditions the entity removed from a MINION owned by a genuine squad player. GW2EI's `ConditionCleanseCount` loops `foreach (Player p in log.PlayerList)` (`SupportStatistics.cs`), so a cleanse landed on a ranger pet, necro minion, mesmer clone or revenant spirit is counted ZERO times; the in-game arcdps meter folds pets into their master and does count them, which is the whole reason arcdps reads a few percent higher than EI for the same fight (two independent field reports of the gap: +3.3% and +4.1%). Kept as a SEPARATE counter, never folded into `cleanses`, so every EI-calibrated number stays bit-identical -- `support_matches_ei_golden` passes unchanged. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.5.1 baseline: purely additive, exactly 42 diffs, every one an ADDED `cleanses_minions` key, nothing removed and not one existing value moved. byteLength grew by 1386 = 42 x 33. Measured on axibridge's testdata/20260128-190427.zevtc the new bucket is +3.85% squad-wide (+2.1%..+5.2% per player), independently corroborated by a raw-EVTC probe that decoded the same log's BuffRemoveAll events and recovered the same per-player minion counts. Regenerated for the MNAME skill-name-resolution fix, Task 1: CatalogBuilder::finish gained access to the log's own `cbtskill` table (`Metrics::log_skill_names`) and now delegates to `skill_map::resolve_name` -- its full four-rung chain -- instead of running a second, shorter chain that consulted neither the log table nor `pseudo_name`. `blocks.healing` and other non-skill_map blocks reference ids skill_map's damage/rotation scope never covers, and those used to fall straight through to the GW2 API catalog or the "Skill <id>" placeholder. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.6.0 baseline: purely additive, exactly 48 changed leaves, every one a `catalogs.skills.*.name`, every one from a `Skill <id>` placeholder to a real name now resolved from the log's own skill table (id 13721 -> Restorative Mantras among them, the MNAME report's own reduced example), none in the other direction, nothing added or removed. byteLength grew by 184. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for the MNAME skill-name-resolution fix, Task 4: `skill_map::resolve_name` now consults GW2EI's `OverridenSkillNames` table (`skill_name_overrides::name`, generated in Task 3) as its new last rung, below `skill_icons::name` and above the final `"Skill <id>"` placeholder. Precedence was MEASURED, not assumed: ranking the override table FIRST (matching GW2EI's own `SkillItem.cs`) was implemented and measured against `fixtures/local/wvw-postrework.zevtc` in `tests/name_override_precedence.rs` -- it renamed 17 ids the log table already resolved (e.g. `"Flame Blast"` -> `"Flame Blast (Minor/Major/Superior Sigil of Fire)"`) against only 2 ids it actually fixed from the placeholder, which exceeds the 5-id budget `resolve_name`'s doc comment sets for adopting GW2EI's disambiguation preference, so the table was demoted to last-resort instead, where it can only ever displace the placeholder. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.6.0-Task-1 baseline on `fixtures/wvw-small.anon.zevtc`: exactly ONE changed leaf, `catalogs.skills.1066.name`, from `"Skill 1066"` to `"Resurrect"` (id 1066 is the MNAME report's own headline example: arcdps writes the literal numeric placeholder `"1066"` for it and `/v2/skills` has no entry at all, so the override table is its only name source); nothing added, nothing removed. byteLength shrank by 1 (`"Resurrect"` is one byte shorter than `"Skill 1066"`). Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests, and the pre-change build (worktree at commit 842ddcb) reproduced the previous baseline digest (dcbbc25e...) byte for byte. Regenerated for the MNAME skill-name-resolution fix, Task 5: `blocks.healing`'s indirect (healing-over-time) rows now additionally register in the buff catalog (`cats.reference_buff`, alongside the existing `cats.reference_skill` -- a deliberate superset, not a replacement, on the same reasoning already documented for Stun/Daze), and `BuffEntry::name` falls through the same shared chain `SkillEntry::name` already uses (`metrics.skill_map` then `skill_map::resolve_name`) instead of `buffs::name(id).unwrap_or_default()`, which emitted the EMPTY string for any id outside the boon/condition/control tables. GW2EI's own `BuildHealingDist` routes an indirect row's id into `buffMap`, a direct row's into `skillMap` -- verified against `fixtures/local/wvw-postrework.ei.json`, where 13721 and 77020 are buffs while 1066 and 53183 are skills. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.6.0-Task-4 baseline (worktree at commit 28f5ad3 reproduced it byte for byte first): purely ADDITIVE, exactly 60 new leaves, nothing removed, nothing changed -- 15 new `catalogs.buffs.<id>` entries (name/kind/stacking always present, icon on 13 of 15, max_stacks on 2 of 15), every `name` a real GW2 buff name (e.g. 13721 -> Restorative Mantras, the same id Task 1's regeneration named on the skill side; none of the 15 came out empty), every `kind` "effect" (none of the 15 collide with the boon or condition tables, so the fallback never overrides them). byteLength grew by 3219 (8621579 - 8618360). Re-digested (byteLength UNCHANGED at 8621579) for the 1.6.1 version bump, the same mechanism as the 1.2.0 re-digest recorded above: the document embeds `axilog.version`, and "1.6.0" and "1.6.1" are the same byte length, so the content moved without the length moving -- which is exactly the failure the test reported ("length matched but the digest did not"). Proven to be the version string and nothing else BEFORE regenerating: a leaf-by-leaf machine diff of the pre-bump capture against the post-bump capture over all 206152 leaves found 0 added, 0 removed, and exactly 1 changed -- `.axilog.version` '1.6.0' -> '1.6.1'. No catalogs, blocks or entities leaf moved. Determinism verified: two independent release-build captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for the MNAME symbol-name rung: `skill_map::resolve_name` gained a fifth and final named rung, `skill_symbol_names::name`, generated by `scripts/gen_skill_symbol_name_catalog.py` from every `const long` in GW2EI's `SkillIDs.cs` (5,568 positive ids, de-camel-cased -- `GladiatorsDefenseAnimation` -> "Gladiators Defense Animation"). It ranks BELOW the log table, the pseudo names, the GW2 API catalog and `skill_name_overrides`, and immediately above the `"Skill <id>"` placeholder, so like rungs 3 and 4 it is additive by construction: it can only displace the placeholder, never a name a higher-authority rung produced (guarded directly by `symbol_rung_never_displaces_a_higher_rung`, which walks all 5,568 entries and asserts both that a log name wins and that any id the API catalog or override table knows keeps that name). The rung exists because a symbol is not a display name and the bar at this position is not "good name vs. better name" but "de-camel-cased symbol vs. Skill 23288": measured against the reporter-scale evidence -- a real ~4,000-log WvW corpus, swept through axibridge's own parse path -- 22 distinct ids still rendered as the literal placeholder after Task 4's override rung landed, and one generated table closes 14 of them at once, including the four Weaver dual-attunement ids (41166/42264/43470/44857) this project had already ledgered as a known gap needing a bespoke `WeaverHelper.cs` port. The remaining 8 have no symbol in either source and correctly keep the placeholder. Regenerated for `analysis::arcdps_parity`, a second cleanse/strip pass alongside (never folded into) the EI-calibrated one in `analysis::support`: six new always-on fields on every `blocks.support.by_entity` row (`cleanses_arcdps`, `cleanses_arcdps_by_minion`, `cleanses_arcdps_on_minion` and the three `strips_arcdps*` twins), plus the matching `condiCleanseArcdps*`/`boonStripsArcdps*` keys on the EI-shaped export. The pass is a transcription of the arcdps meter's OWN counting code, pasted into Discord by deltaconnected on 2026-08-26: stability only counts when more than one stack came off, self-consumed blind never counts, the condition dump a player takes on going down is subtracted back out, pets fold into their master, and there is no squad/non-squad discrimination anywhere. It is THREE buckets rather than one because the number the in-game meter displays depends on that window's "vs npcs"/"from npcs" toggles, which the reader sets and this pass refuses to guess; on this fixture the buckets are 900/46/157, so the toggle choice moves the total by 26%. The load-bearing evidence that the transcription is right is that the toggle-independent base lands at 900 against EI's `condiCleanse + condiCleanseSelf` of 898 -- a prediction it could easily have failed, made against a number nobody tuned it to -- and that the "vs npcs" bucket comes out at exactly the 46 the independently-derived `cleanses_minions` counter finds by a different route. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.6.2 baseline: 206152 leaves before, 206404 after, purely ADDITIVE -- exactly 252 added (42 entities x 6 keys), 0 removed and 0 CHANGED, so not one EI-calibrated value moved, which is the whole design constraint. byteLength grew by 9536. Determinism verified: two independent release-build captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests, and the pre-change build (worktree at 2476cc1) reproduced the previous baseline digest (630f7d3a...) byte for byte. Regenerated for `blocks.damage_mods.personal` (and the EI-shaped export's top-level `personalDamageMods`): the spec -> ids partition of `damageModMap` that says which rows are a player's OWN trait/skill modifiers and which belong to the shared pool -- relics, food, squad buffs -- whose gain every benefiting player is credited with. GW2EI has always emitted it (`JsonLogBuilder.cs:315`) and this project never did, and the omission was not cosmetic: an EI-shaped consumer that reads the empty set as "nothing is personal" rather than as "unclassified" filters every modifier away, which is exactly what blanked axibridge's Damage Modifiers panel for every natively parsed log (reported 2026-08-26). The classification rule is GW2EI's own and the `SpecSpecificShared` subtlety is reproduced with it: EI tests the descriptor's `Srcs`, not the source bucket the container filed the modifier under, so a `.UsingSpecSpecificShared()` modifier is offered to everyone yet counts as personal only for its own spec. Calibrated against the reference export (`fixtures/local/wvw-postrework.ei.json`, EI 3.27.0.0): same 14 spec keys, and on all 69 ids both engines emit, ZERO classification disagreements in either direction. The 6 ids the export calls personal that we do not are ids this engine's catalog never emits at all -- a pre-existing coverage gap, asserted as such rather than tolerated. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the pre-change build (worktree at d010da6): 206404 leaves before, 206457 after, purely ADDITIVE -- exactly 53 added, every one a `.blocks.damage_mods.personal.*` id, 0 removed and 0 CHANGED. byteLength grew by 1207. Determinism verified: two independent release-build captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. This regeneration ALSO absorbs a re-digest the v1.7.0 release bump missed: the document embeds `axilog.version`, "1.6.2" and "1.7.0" are the same byte length, so the previous baseline was already red on main with the length matching and the digest not. Proven rather than assumed before regenerating: the pre-change capture contains exactly ONE occurrence of "1.7.0", and substituting "1.6.2" back for it reproduces the previous baseline digest (004458f0...) byte for byte, so nothing else in the document had moved.
